body:
[aida:reviewer] PR #1989 REVIEWED — REQUEST-CHANGES at 20881480b8. It was the only PR
tonight held purely for want of a review, and it is now held on a verdict instead.
Three findings; one is blocking, one needs a decision from you, one is coordination.

INDEPENDENCE: I authored none of the three commits. My session has made zero commits.
Two are [AI:claude] from another seat, one [AI:codex]. Build (ubuntu-latest) PASSES at
10m39s; the only red check is merge-hold-gate, which is the hold.

THE SPLIT ITSELF IS SOUND and I want to say that before the findings. Dispatch is
routing and disposition is judgement, and gating them separately is right. Extending
queue remove and queue move to dispatch authority - mutations that were ungated - is a
tightening nobody asked for and it is correct.

F1 BLOCKING: A HALF-FINISHED REMOVAL LEAVES A DEAD CONFIG KEY ADVERTISED IN --help.

The PR deletes BOTH production enforcement sites for GatedOp::DrainStart - lib.rs:49491
and queue_cmd.rs:5278. I grepped main; those are the only two. Afterwards the enum
variant, its config-key mapping to "drain_start", its description and its test all
remain in permissions.rs with nothing calling them.

So [team.permissions] drain_start becomes a key that silently does nothing. And
cli.rs:2175 still reads "Bypass the team RBAC guardrail ([team.permissions]
drain_start)" - --help text advertising a guardrail this PR removes.

Either direction is acceptable, neither is: keep the config consulted alongside
has_dispatch_authority, or remove the variant, key, description, test and help text in
this change. A config key with no reader is worse than none, because the user believes
it works.

I checked the --force parity specifically and it is NOT a finding: handle_burndown_run
preserves it as `!force && !has_dispatch_authority()`, and queue_cmd passed false before
and gates unconditionally now. Same behaviour.

F2 NEEDS YOUR DECISION, AND IT LANDS ON TONIGHT'S WORK.

merge-hold Clear now requires has_integrity_floor_authority() = stdin().is_terminal().
A HUMAN AT A TTY. The message says dispatch or advisor authority cannot override it.

So an agent reviewer cannot clear a hold it placed itself. Three of the 24 markers are
mine and say "clear only on my re-review". After this lands I could re-review, approve,
and be unable to withdraw my own refusal.

That contradicts the convention you recorded on TASK-1-170 tonight - a hold is cleared
by the seat whose refusal it carries. If the integrity floor is the intent, TASK-1-170
needs amending in the same change and reviewer holds need another release path.

THE SHARPER PROBLEM IS THE ORDERING AGAINST BUG-1532. pr ship clears a hold today with
no TTY at all (pr_cmd.rs:1793, deliberate under BUG-1167). So this PR locks the
SUPPORTED release path while the BYPASS stays open: until BUG-1532 lands, the only way
an agent seat can clear a hold is the unsafe one. I am not asking for BUG-1532 to be
fixed here - I am asking that this not land before it, or that it land with the ordering
stated.

F3 COORDINATION — AND IT PARTLY SETTLES MY OWN HELD PR.

This PR adds a status gate to tool_queue_rework_inner at mcp.rs:4146-4151, keyed on the
COMPUTED target. That is exactly item 1b of my blocking finding on PR #2035 - the
ungated Draft to Approved promotion reachable from MCP. It is done correctly: gating the
computed target means it survives #2035 replacing rework_smart_target with
rework_target_for_mode.

Two consequences. The two PRs touch the same function and WILL conflict - whichever
lands second must preserve this gate rather than reverting it while resolving. And
#2035's item 1a, the CLI path in handle_queue_rework which still flips status through
update_atomically with no authority check, is NOT covered by it. I will state that on
#2035's rework so the brief does not imply both legs are outstanding when one is being
fixed elsewhere.

THE HOLD STAYS, now on my refusal rather than on your withdrawn clauses. I have not
touched the marker or the label.

ONE OBSERVATION ABOUT THE PR ITSELF: commit a4b0aa2491 regenerates
docs/architecture/external-tool-output-classifiers.md. That is the BUG-1526 remedy being
applied by hand, three commits into an unrelated PR - which is the line-number churn
predicted, showing up as noise in a change about authority. Not a finding against this
PR; evidence for BUG-1526's priority.
subject: PR #1989 REQUEST-CHANGES at 20881480b8: drain_start left as a dead config key still advertised in --help; merge-hold clear becomes TTY-only which strands agent reviewer holds (ordering vs BUG-1532)
